messages:
michael: Quick postmortem notewe saw a canary flip-flop yesterday when late observer verdicts arrived after the decider already shifted traffic.

michael: TL;DR: observer emits low-level alerts, decider applies a change, then stale alert arrives -> extra rollback + churn. Need a clean contract to avoid ordering problems.

tara: Can you outline what data the observer currently sends?

michael: It's very lightweight: <verdict, metric_name, value, timestamp>. No notion of which rollout decision the probe was evaluating.

ji: Problem sounds like lack of causality. We could add a small rollout lease token that the decider issues when a rollout epoch starts; observers include that token in subsequent verdicts. If token doesn't match current lease, decider ignores the verdict.

rachel: That feels straightforward. Alternatives: (A) let observers keep emitting raw events and make the decider do heavy deduping/origin correlation, or (B) push more intelligence to observers so they wait for a lease before reporting. I prefer lightweight lease token - keeps observers cheap.

tara: How would the lease work in practice? details pls.

ji: Sketch: - Decider increments rollout_epoch and mints lease_id (short hex). - Decision payload contains {action, rollout_epoch, seq, ttl, hint_set}. - Observers attach the last seen lease_id / epoch to their verdicts. - Decider ignores verdicts whose epoch < current_epoch or whose lease_id != active lease (unless we have backward-compatibility flag).

michael: Important: keep parity for older observer SDKs. If observer sends no epoch, treat it as best-effort but lower-confidence. Maybe require aggregator nodes to stamp epoch if available.

rachel: Another angle: expand the decision to include a tiny ranked fallback list so runtime has choices. If the decider says "fallback preferred", runtime gets a list of ordered fallbacks (e.g., [A-model, q8-variant, regional-pool]) and picks the first compatible. That decouples the decider's notion of "what to do" from the runtime's notion of "how to do it cheaply."

tara: Agree but watch out for perf: keep rank lists short (<=3) and encoded compactly. We can't have the runtime iterate huge lists on hot path.

ji: Also add a small reason code and a local score to each hint so runtime can break ties (score 0..100). Example hint: model:A, score:95, reason:p95>300ms.

michael: Observability: every decision should emit a commit event with epoch, seq, applied_percent, and trace_id. That way we can query timeline: decision X -> signals Y -> user impact Z. Useful for debugging flaps.

ops-bot: deploy: rollout-decider v0.4 -> canary started eu-central-1 5% :rocket:

rachel: Action items: - michael: PR to add epoch/lease field to observer SDK + backcompat guard - tara: perf microbenchmark for hint-list application in runtime - ji: short RFC for minor decision payload changes (seq/ttl/hints) and durable log option later - all: define telemetry event fields and add a quick e2e that injects late verdicts to validate ignore-path.

michael: Timeline: ship lease_id epoch change as a small opt-in toggle in next patch release. Don't block on a durable decision-plane for now; we can add an append-only commit log in a follow-up cycle.

tara: One more thought: in high-QPS customers observers may still produce many stale verdicts. Add cheap sampling and let aggregators compress repeated identical verdicts into a single stamped event. That lowers bandwidth and reduces race surface.

ji: For the longer term, propose a decision-plane that serializes commits so ordering is explicit and replayable. But operationally we get a lot by just adding epoch/lease + seq + TTL.

rachel: I'll draft the compatibility matrix for SDKs and runtime versions and include a small test harness.

michael: Thanks all. This should remove the main source of flip-flop without big infra changes. Ping if you want to pair on the PR.
